title: Namespaces and Dependency Design
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of namespaces and dependency design and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply importing functions in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Namespaces and Dependency Design is part of R Packages and Package Development. Start with importing functions and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: A maintainable R package needs clear metadata, namespaces, dependencies, documentation, tests and checks before release.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: A maintainable R package needs clear metadata, namespaces, dependencies, documentation, tests and checks before release. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Importing Functions
items.text: Build the smallest example for importing functions, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

items.title: Exporting Public Functions
items.text: Build the smallest example for exporting public functions, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

items.title: Internal Functions
items.text: Use internal functions to make input, output and scope explicit, then test both a typical call and one edge case.

items.title: Declaring Package Dependencies
items.text: Explain declaring package dependencies in the context of namespaces and dependency design, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Avoiding Unnecessary Dependencies
items.text: Explain avoiding unnecessary dependencies in the context of namespaces and dependency design, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Designing Stable APIs
items.text: For designing stable apis, describe the trust boundary, input checks, failure handling and cleanup; keep credentials and real private data out of examples.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Identify the package files involved and name one test or check that should pass before publishing. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: Do not claim a package is ready to publish until clean-environment checks pass. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For namespaces and dependency design, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on a package attached only in the interactive workspace.
common_mistakes.why: A clean session may not have that dependency attached or installed.
common_mistakes.fix: Declare imports and test package functions from a fresh R session.

common_mistakes.problem: Publishing examples without running their tests or checks.
common_mistakes.why: Documentation can be stale and examples can fail on a clean machine.
common_mistakes.fix: Run package tests and R CMD check under the supported R version.

common_mistakes.problem: Leaving dependencies and version assumptions undocumented.
common_mistakes.why: Users may not be able to reproduce the package behavior.
